office_does: A Benton PUD commissioner sits on the three-member elected board of the public electric utility serving about 59,000 customers in Kennewick, Finley, Benton City, Prosser and rural Benton County, for a six-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat: longtime Commissioner Jeff Hall is not on the ballot, and every Benton PUD voter, not just District 2, votes in November. Agricultural executive Dewey Holliday stresses financial oversight and weighing every power source on reliability and cost. Kennewick School Board member Micah Valentine runs against state clean-energy mandates and for dams, nuclear and low rates.

candidates.summary: Prosser agricultural executive, irrigators-association president and appointed West Benton Fire and Rescue commissioner, running on financial oversight, infrastructure planning and reliable, affordable power.
highlights: Managed more than $70 million a year in farm operating and capital budgets; president of the Columbia Snake River Irrigators Association [S1]
Wants hydropower to stay the backbone and would weigh every option, including small modular reactors, on reliability, cost and risk [S2][S3]
Says large new loads such as data centers should pay their own way without existing customers subsidizing them [S3]
Endorsed by the Washington and Benton County Farm Bureaus and Teamsters Local 839 [S2]

candidates.summary: Kennewick School Board member in his second term and local business owner, running against Olympia energy mandates and for dams, nuclear power and low rates.
highlights: Second-term Kennewick School Board director; says he helped oversee a $330 million district budget [S1]
Opposes reliance on wind and solar and state energy mandates; supports protecting dams and expanding nuclear [S1][S2]
Would back a natural gas plant or small nuclear reactor and pledges hard questions before spending [S2]
Endorsed by the Benton County Republican Party; campaigns as a conservative in this nonpartisan race [S3][S4]
